ov: A burrowing, nocturnal African mammal that digs out ants and termites with powerful claws and collects them with a long, sticky tongue. It’s the only living member of its order, related to elephants and manatees.

why.et: Some people hunt aardvarks for meat.

rg: Much of the southern two-thirds of Africa, avoiding rocky areas.

cf.tip: The aardvark is sometimes called an anteater, but it isn’t related to the South American anteaters.

fx: Its name is Afrikaans for “earth pig”.
notes: The existing fact is half confirmed: up to 50,000 insects in a night is recorded, and it "can dig extremely quickly", but the team with shovels isn’t in the article. Suggested wording: "Can eat up to 50,000 ants and termites in a single night." RESOLVED (owner: approve all): fact rewritten as suggested.
